original_title: The future of the Elder Scrolls Online looks rocky after culling of leadership team
summary_en: The Elder Scrolls Online studio has seen a significant shake-up with over 200 staff laid off, including key leadership. This drastic measure follows a pattern of workforce reduction, leaving many to wonder about the game's long-term trajectory.

en.title: Elder Scrolls Online Leadership Culling Raises Questions About Its Future
en.summary: The Elder Scrolls Online studio has seen a significant shake-up with over 200 staff laid off, including key leadership. This drastic measure follows a pattern of workforce reduction, leaving many to wonder about the game's long-term trajectory.
en.body:
The vibrant world of **The Elder Scrolls Online** is facing an uncertain future following a substantial wave of layoffs that have impacted its development studio, ZeniMax Online. Reports indicate that over 200 employees have been let go, a move that has seen the departure of long-serving studio leadership. Among those departing is studio head **Joseph Burba**, who has been with ZeniMax Online for 14 years and instrumental since the game's 2014 launch. Also leaving their roles are executive producer **Susan Kath**, game director **Rich Lambert**, and production director **Ala Diaz**. These individuals are expected to remain with the studio for a few months to facilitate a leadership transition.

This significant reduction in staff, which has seen the studio lose at least 40% of its workforce since late 2024, raises serious concerns about institutional knowledge and the continuity of development. While an internal memo expressed confidence in the incoming leadership, **Nick Giacomini** and **Josh Henderson**, the scale of these layoffs is unprecedented for the studio. The departure of figures like **Joseph Burba**, who has been a cornerstone of **ESO** for over a decade, represents a considerable loss of experience. The memo itself attempts to reassure the remaining staff and the community, stating, "With exciting experiences still ahead for our players as we wrap up work for Update 51 and beyond, we believe that your passion, creativity, and commitment to each other and the community will continue serving as the heartbeat of ESO."

## Community Concerns Grow

The ramifications of these cuts are keenly felt by the passionate **Elder Scrolls Online** community. For many players, the stability and vision of the development team are directly tied to their investment in Tamriel's vast world. The sheer number of layoffs, coupled with the removal of core leadership, has inevitably led to discussions about the game's long-term support and future content roadmap. While some online discussions express cautious optimism, citing past resilience and confidence in the remaining team, a palpable sense of unease pervades fan forums and social media. The move is widely seen as a cost-saving measure by Microsoft, following its acquisition of ZeniMax Media, but the impact on morale and the potential loss of vital creative direction are significant worries for those who have dedicated years to the game.

## What's Next for Tamriel?

With new leadership stepping in and a substantial portion of the team gone, the immediate focus will be on navigating the transition and delivering upcoming content, including **Update 51**. How ZeniMax Online will adapt and continue to innovate in **The Elder Scrolls Online**'s crowded MMORPG landscape, especially with a significantly smaller workforce, remains to be seen. Players will be watching closely for any signs of how these changes will affect the game's ongoing narrative, gameplay updates, and overall player experience in the coming months and years.

es.title: El futuro de The Elder Scrolls Online en duda tras una oleada de despidos
es.summary: El estudio de The Elder Scrolls Online ha sufrido una gran reestructuración con más de 200 empleados despedidos, incluyendo a figuras clave de la dirección. Esta medida drástica sigue un patrón de reducción de personal, lo que deja a muchos preguntándose sobre la trayectoria a largo plazo del juego. La comunidad de jugadores se muestra preocupada por el impacto que esto pueda tener en el futuro del juego.
es.body:
El vibrante mundo de **The Elder Scrolls Online** se enfrenta a un futuro incierto tras una oleada de despidos que han afectado a su estudio de desarrollo, ZeniMax Online. Según informes, más de 200 empleados han sido despedidos, lo que ha supuesto la partida de veteranos líderes del estudio. Entre los que dejan sus puestos se encuentran el jefe de estudio **Joseph Burba**, quien llevaba 14 años en ZeniMax Online y ha sido fundamental desde el lanzamiento del juego en 2014. También dejan sus roles la productora ejecutiva **Susan Kath**, el director del juego **Rich Lambert** y el director de producción **Ala Diaz**. Se espera que estos individuos permanezcan en el estudio durante unos meses para facilitar una transición de liderazgo.

 
   Esta reducción significativa del personal, que ha visto al estudio perder al menos el 40% de su plantilla desde finales de 2024, plantea serias preocupaciones sobre el conocimiento institucional y la continuidad del desarrollo. Aunque un memo interno expresó confianza en el liderazgo entrante, **Nick Giacomini** y **Josh Henderson**, el alcance de estos despidos es sin precedentes para el estudio. La partida de figuras como **Joseph Burba**, que ha sido un pilar de **ESO** durante más de una década, representa una pérdida considerable de experiencia.

 
   ## Preocupaciones de la comunidad
 
   Las ramificaciones de estos recortes se sienten profundamente en la apasionada comunidad de **The Elder Scrolls Online**. Para muchos jugadores, la estabilidad y visión del equipo de desarrollo están directamente relacionadas con su inversión en el vasto mundo de Tamriel. La gran cantidad de despidos, unida a la eliminación de la dirección central, ha llevado inevitablemente a discusiones sobre el soporte a largo plazo del juego y su hoja de ruta de contenido futuro. Mientras que algunas discusiones en línea expresan una cautelosa optimismo, citando la resistencia pasada y la confianza en el equipo restante, una palpable sensación de inquietud permea los foros de fans y las redes sociales. El movimiento es ampliamente visto como una medida de ahorro de costos por parte de Microsoft, tras su adquisición de ZeniMax Media, pero el impacto en la moral y la posible pérdida de vital dirección creativa son preocupaciones significativas para aquellos que han dedicado años al juego.

 
   ## ¿Qué sigue para Tamriel?
 
   Con el nuevo liderazgo asumiendo el mando y una parte sustancial del equipo ido, el enfoque inmediato será navegar la transición y entregar contenido próximo, incluyendo **Update 51**. Cómo ZeniMax Online se adaptará y seguirá innovando en el paisaje de MMORPG de **The Elder Scrolls Online**, especialmente con una plantilla significativamente más pequeña, queda por verse. Los jugadores estarán observando de cerca cualquier señal de cómo estos cambios afectarán la narrativa en curso del juego, las actualizaciones de juego y la experiencia general del jugador en los próximos meses y años.

content_raw: ZeniMax Online head Joseph Burba is among over 200 staff laid off at the Elder Scrolls Online studio last week as part of Xbox's recent round of mass layoffs . Burba has been with the studio for 14 years, and has worked on The Elder Scrolls Online since its 2014 launch. He was promoted to studio lead in July last year. The news comes via Game File , who obtained a list of roles impacted by Microsoft's recent purge from the state of Maryland, where both ZeniMax Online Studios and its parent company, ZeniMax Media Inc, are based. In addition to Burba, ESO executive producer Susan Kath, game director Rich Lambert, and production director Ala Diaz have all lost their roles. According to documents seen by Game File, all four will remain at the studio for "the next few months" to help transition a new leadership team, which will consist of ESO game lead Nick Giacomini, and business operations lead Josh Henderson. "We have tremendous confidence in Josh and Nick, the future of this studio, and the continued growth of ESO," an internal memo penned by the outgoing leadership read. "With exciting experiences still ahead for our players as we wrap up work for Update 51 and beyond, we believe that your passion, creativity, and commitment to each other and the community will continue serving as the heartbeat of ESO." ZeniMax Online has shrunk considerably since late 2024, when its headcount was roughly 461 if union membership is any indication. After layoffs in 2025 and 2026 the studio has lost at least 40% of its workforce. Lopping off executive staff is probably a quick and easy way to save money, but it also means destroying—especially in the case of Burba—decades worth of institutional knowledge. It's unclear how "growth" will be achieved for ESO in light of how severely the studio's head count has contracted, but according to ESO community manager Kevin Gbolie, writing after news of the layoffs, "the plan is still to deliver great content, and we will hopefully have an update soon." Last week's seismic Microsoft layoffs also impacted ZeniMax Media: of the 379 in total, 213 were from ZeniMax Online Studios, and 166 from ZeniMax Media, the latter including Bethesda Game Studios and Bethesda's publishing concerns.
